title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 70
paragraphs: Having heard what he wished to learn, Demaratus took provisions for the road and set out, pretending that he was going to Delphi to consult the oracle — but his destination was Elis. The Lacedaemonians, suspecting he was trying to escape, set off in pursuit; but before they caught him Demaratus had already crossed from Elis to Zacynthus. The Spartans crossed after him and seized his attendants, though the Zacynthians refused to give up the man himself. From there Demaratus crossed over into Asia, to the court of King Darius, who received him with great honor as a guest and granted him land and cities. That is how Demaratus came to Asia — a man who had distinguished himself among the Lacedaemonians in many ways, by both deeds and counsels, and who, above all, had won them an Olympic victory in the four-horse chariot race, the only king of Sparta ever to do so.
